## TASK: Load libraries

```{r}
# Turn off scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

# Load the tidyverse
library(tidyverse)

# Load janitor
library(janitor)
```

## TASK: Load data and clean up the column names

Load the two datasets we worked with in the pre_lab that are in the data folder: the Maryland payments to vendors and Maryland grants and loans AND, using janitor, change the column names so that they are lower-cased and any spaces are replaced with underscores.

```{r}
payments <- read_csv("data/State_of_Maryland_Payments_Data__FY2008_to_FY2024.csv")

md_grants_loans <- read_csv("data/State_of_Maryland_Grant_and_Loan_Data__FY2009_to_FY2022.csv")
```

```{r}
cleaned_payments <- payments |> clean_names()

#Display that clean ahh data
cleaned_payments
```

```{r}
cleaned_md_grants_loans <- md_grants_loans |> clean_names()

#Display that clean ahh dataset
cleaned_md_grants_loans
```

## Answer questions

Q1: You want to know how much money state agencies have paid to the Prince George's County School system, but to do that you'll need to find all of the variations of how the school system might be listed in the payments data. Look at & search the records in the dataframe to start your search, starting with a broad search and then narrowing it down. Then write code to find rows where the vendor name contains some version of the county's school system.

HINT: you should use filter() just once, and inside your filter you want to look for the variations one at a time. Think "this version OR that version."

When you have found as many as possible, save the result to a new dataframe called `pg_schools`. How many records did you find?

[59 RECORDS]{.underline}

A1:

```{r}
pg_schools <- cleaned_payments |> filter(
  str_detect(vendor_name, "PRINCE GEORGES COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOL") |
  str_detect(vendor_name, "PRINCE GEORGE'S COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOL") |
  str_detect(vendor_name, "PG COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOL") |
  str_detect(vendor_name, "BOARD OF EDUCATION OF PRINCE GEORGE") |
  str_detect(vendor_name, "BOARD OF EDUCATION OF PRINCE GEORGE'S COUNTY") |
  str_detect(vendor_name, "BOARD OF EDUCATION OF PRINCE GEORGES COUNTY MD"))
```

Q2: Using that `pg_schools` dataframe, write code to calculate the total amount of payments to the Prince George's County School system for each fiscal year. Which fiscal year had the largest total amount? Are there any aspects of the results that stand out to you?

**A2:**

**Which fiscal year had the largest total amount?** [2024 did!]{.underline}

**Are there any aspects of the results that stand out to you?** [2016 – a year well-before the covid cost-hike and long after the 08 crash, is randomly in the top 5.]{.underline}

```{r}

pg_schools |> group_by(fiscal_year) |> summarise(amount_in_fiscal_year=sum(amount)) |> arrange(desc(amount_in_fiscal_year))
```

Q3. You're interested in examining the vendors paid for capital projects at the University of Maryland. Search the payments data to find those payments, [then write code to produce a list of each vendor and the total amount it received.]{.underline}

Look carefully at that list - what cleaning will it require to ensure that you have only one row per vendor and zip code? Provide at least three examples of vendor names that are similar and should be combined into one. Describe in words how you might clean that data so that any nearly identical vendors would look identical - what would you change and how?

A3. [I would have to standardize all of the names to be uppercase, and then have similar cells merge using str_to_upper(tktk) from pre-lab 3. If I standardized them, the following duplicate data entries would be merged and not be an issue:]{.underline}

[A MORTON THOMAS & ASSOC INC + A MORTON THOMAS & ASSOCIATES INC \<-- Assoc instead of associates]{.underline}

[A & I INC + A & I INC. \<-- the period makes the error]{.underline}

[AMTEK COMPANY INC + AMTEK COMPANY, INC. \<-- that damn comma. I hate when companies do this.]{.underline}

```{r}
cleaned_payments |> filter(
  str_detect(agency_name, "CAPITAL PROJECTS- UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND")) |> 
  group_by(vendor_name) |> summarise(total_amount = sum(amount)) |> arrange(vendor_name)
```

Q4: You want to understand how much state grant money went to stem cell research projects each fiscal year. Search the data to find grants that fit that description. Once you find which column(s) contain the information you want, your code should find just the grants for stem cell research in a single filter. Then calculate the total amount of money for each fiscal year. Write a sentence summarizing how stem cell research funding has changed over time.

[A4: Stem cell research started getting funding in 2020, decreased a tad bit in 2021 – likely due to pandemic – returned to its average amount in 2022, and then made a massive jump in funding going into 2023.]{.underline}

```{r}
cleaned_md_grants_loans |> filter(str_detect(description, "STEM CELL")) |> group_by(fiscal_year) |> summarise(total_amount = sum(amount)) |> arrange(desc(fiscal_year))
```

Q5: Using the Maryland grants and loan data, find records where the zip code is the one where the University of Maryland-College Park is located in and produce a list of grantees from that zip code, along with the total amount they received. Write a paragraph explaining how many grantees are there, what you would need to do to clean the results so that you had one record per grantee and which grantees are most interesting to you?

[A5: There are 51 grantees but several are the same institution (or basically the same) listed differently (like UMD vs University of Maryland, College Park) and the two different UMD foundation names. str_to_upper() would correct the ones that are different capitalization-wise but the case_when() tool would match the ones with differing names to be combined into one name. Plus on those ones I could confirm that they are NOT two separate organiazations using zip codes and then merge them. I think the most interesting resule is "Ikea - College Park - Solar Canopy' because why the hell does an IKEA (multi-billion-dollar private company btw) need a state grant?]{.underline}

*Write a paragraph explaining how many grantees are there, what you would need to do to clean the results so that you had one record per grantee and which grantees are most interesting to you?*

```{r}
cleaned_md_grants_loans |> filter(str_detect(zip_code, "20740") | str_detect(zip_code, "20741") | str_detect(zip_code, "20742")) |> group_by(grantee) |> summarise(total_amount = sum(amount)) |> arrange(desc(total_amount))
```
